{{Quote|The art of Teräs Käsi is about control and mastery of one's self.|[[Joclad Danva/Legends|Joclad Danva]]|<ref name="HolonetNews">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|sports/1359_1.html|Jedi Defeated for Teräs Käsi Title}}</ref>}}
'''Teräs Käsi''', or "steel hand" in [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]], was a deadly and mystical [[Unarmed combat/Legends|martial art]] discipline renowned throughout the galaxy for its lethality.

==History==
Teräs Käsi originated in the remote star cluster of the [[Pacanth Reach/Legends|Pacanth Reach]] on the world of [[Bunduki/Legends|Bunduki]], which was populated by the near-human species known as the [[Epicanthix]].<ref name="HEROGUIDE">''[[Hero's Guide]]''</ref> On Bunduki, the secretive [[Followers of Palawa]] developed Teräs Käsi to fight the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] after their homeworld of [[Palawa]] was destroyed in a war involving the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]].<ref name="JvS" /> The knowledge of Teräs Käsi resulted in many Followers of Palawa falling to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|Dark side of the Force]].<ref name="tep">{{GamerCite|5|The Emperor's Pawns}}</ref>

To learn Teräs Käsi, students were often sent to learn directly from the Followers, where students were taught about history, literature, metaphysics, and the philosophies of the Pacanth Reach cultures, with the Followers encouraging students to use the art for the good and betterment of society.<ref name="SHADOWS">''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> Many who learned the secrets of Teräs Käsi brought the knowledge to other corners of the galaxy - though it remained rare enough that to learn Teräs Käsi off of Bunduki, one had to seek out one of these graduate masters.<ref name="POWER" />

==Characteristics==
[[File:Defensivestance.png|thumb|left|A Teräs Käsi [[Defensive Stance]] detailing a Nerve Strike.]]
Teräs Käsi practitioners were the undisputed masters of melee combat, their skill and prowess rivaling even that of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. Utilizing ancient meditative techniques, practitioners were capable of pushing their bodies to supernatural limits, achieving the seemingly impossible by mastering mind over body. Masters of the art used extremely quick and devastating strikes, with many of the moves being so fast that the artist appears to blur with speed.<ref name="SECRETS">''{{SonyCite|url=players/guides.vm?id=80131|text=Unlocking the Secrets: A Guide to Role-Playing a Teräs Käsi Artist}}'' This players guide uses quotes about Teras Kasi straight from Star Wars Galaxies as a resource for players after the NGE (New Game Enhancement), when Teräs Käsi ceased to be an initial class in Galaxies.</ref><ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesAED}} From in-game text, missions, etcetera. Please note that Teras Kasi was an initial class upon release, but was eliminated after the NGE or "New Game Enhancement".</ref>

A deadly and exceedingly lethal martial art, Teräs Käsi actually meant "steel hands" in Basic, referring to the extreme toughness of a practitioner's fists and the heavy piston-like blows they could produce.<ref name="HEROGUIDE" /> This reputation was well deserved; masters of Teräs Käsi were known to deliver strikes that rivaled [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrowers]] and [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]] in terms of power,<ref name="THREATS">''[[Threats of the Galaxy]]'' Based on a 2d10 & 3d10 damage output by a Teras Kasi Master in Threats, which is equivalent to the damage output of slugthrowers and pistols within the same source.</ref> easily punching through body armor, with even novitiates capable of surprising damage - though to a somewhat lesser degree.<ref name="HEROGUIDE damage">''[[Hero's Guide]]'', based on a 4d4 damage output, equivalent to a pistol within the same source.</ref> Further, intense training in Teräs Käsi could develop a blinding speed and tune the senses so accurately that a practitioner could anticipate strikes with an uncanny ease, being able to dodge so quickly that they appeared as a blur.<ref name="EP3PRIMA">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'': Prima Official Game Guide]] The Prima guide explicitly states that clone assassins were intensely trained in Teräs Käsi, and that it is Teräs Käsi and not genetic alterations that gave them their speed.</ref><ref name="CWCG">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]'' The campaign guide confirms this "blinding speed", as well as clone assassins martial art training.</ref> As a result, practitioners also had a high degree of acrobatics; a falling practitioner could use midair acrobatics to direct their fall and avoid striking ledges and other potentially lethal obstructions.<ref name="Shadow Hunter">''[[Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter]]''</ref>

These feats of strength, speed, and acrobatics were made possible due to the central tenets of Teräs Käsi, mainly control and mastery of one's self,<ref name="HolonetNews" /> to the point that a practitioner had complete control over their body.<ref name="Shadow Hunter" /> Teräs Käsi also incorporated meditative arts, turning a Teräs Käsi artist's mental control inwards rather than outwards; practitioners could enter an immobile meditative trance-like state and stop bleeding, as well as slow poisons and diseases - master meditation artists were even able to slowly heal their own wounds by channeling their mental energies back into themselves.<ref name="GALAXPRIMA">[[Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]] As defined by the "Meditate" skill in SWG. It should be noted this is pre-NGE (New Game Enhancement), when Teräs Käsi was an initial class in ''Galaxies''.</ref> As a martial art, Teräs Käsi was patterned after the movements and hunting characteristics of various beasts throughout the galaxy, with many moves being named after these movements - such as [[Charging Wampa]], [[Rancor Rising]], and [[Dancing Dragonsnake]] to name a few.<ref name="Shadow Hunter" /><ref name="POWER" /> Teräs Käsi emphasized close work, utilizing hands, feet, elbows, blades, and sticks, with half a dozen basic stances that relied on four ranges of engagement; kicking, punching, elbowing, and grappling range.<ref name="DEATHSTAR">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref>

==Notable Practitioners==
[[File:Pike_sisters.jpg|thumb|220px|The Pike sisters: [[Zan Pike|Zan]] and [[Zu Pike|Zu]], masters of Teräs Käsi]]
Lending to its initial creation as a weapon against [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], Teräs Käsi was exceedingly lethal, and allowed dedicated practitioners an incredibly high degree of combat skill. For example, the non-[[Force-sensitive/Legends|forceful]] Pike sisters defeated over two dozen armed combatants single-handedly using only Teras Kasi, ultimately refusing to use weapons, and were fully capable of taking out squads of opponents armed with [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]].<ref name="RebSOURCE">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Phow Ji, a non-[[Force-sensitive/Legends|forceful]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenary]] and Teräs Käsi practitioner from [[Bunduki/Legends|Bunduki]] singlehandedly engaged a large group of [[Salissian/Legends|Salissian]] mercenaries and [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]], showing immense martial ability in the process, and was capable of drawing his weapons so fast that they seemed to simply appear in his hands, firing his [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] so accurately as to shoot his opponents [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]] out of their hands, and largely avoiding blaster fire from dozens of infantry with acrobatic leaps, feints, and dodges described as "Jedi-like".<ref name="Battle Surgeons">''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]''</ref>

Some [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] duelists used Teräs Käsi techniques in combat, most notably [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], who trained extensively in the art and incorporated it into his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] and unarmed techniques - Maul credited the martial art as one of the primary reasons he was so successful and deadly as an assassin. Some Jedi also studied Teräs Käsi, including [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Anoon Bondara]],<ref name="Shadow Hunter" /> [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Joclad Danva/Legends|Joclad Danva]],<ref name="HolonetNews" /> and [[Bultar Swan/Legends|Bultar Swan]].<ref name="ballgame">{{SW|url=news/take-me-out-to-the-ballgame-sports-in-the-star-wars-galaxy-part-2|series=Sports in the Star Wars Galaxy|text=Part 2: Take Me Out to the Ball Game|nolive=1}}</ref>

==Known moves==
*[[Aryx slash]] was named after the [[Aryx/Legends|aryx]] of [[Cerea/Legends|Cerea]].
*[[Charging Wampa]] was named after the [[Wampa/Legends|Wampa]] of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. The move involved charging at your opponent, attempting to hit them in the jaw, followed by a simultaneous hit of both arms on the opponent's neck.
*[[Dancing Dragonsnake]] was named after the [[Dragonsnake/Legends|Dragonsnake]] of [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]].
*[[Death Weave]]
*[[Förräderi]]
*[[Gorax smash]] was named after the gigantic [[Gorax/Legends|gorax]] species.
*[[Gronda stomp]] was named after the [[Corellia/Legends|Corellian]] [[gronda]].
*[[Gundark slap]] was named after the [[Gundark/Legends|gundark]] species.
*[[Leaping veermok]] was named after the leaping movement of the [[Veermok/Legends|veermok]].
*[[Nerve strike]]<ref name="SWG" />
*[[Nexu Grin]] was named after the [[Nexu/Legends|nexu]] of [[Cholganna/Legends|Cholganna]].
*[[Rancor Rising]] was named after the [[Rancor/Legends|rancor]] of [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]].
*[[Riding Bantha]] was named after the [[Bantha/Legends|beast of burden of the same name]].
*[[Screaming squill]] was named after the scream of the [[Squill (creature)|squill]].
*[[Shenbit bonecrusher blow]] was named after the [[shenbit bonecrusher]].
*[[Slashing Wampa]] was named after the [[Wampa/Legends|wampa]] of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].
*[[Sleeping krayt]] was named after the dangerous [[Krayt dragon/Legends|krayt dragon]].
*[[Spitting Rawl Technique]] was reputed to be the most powerful attack in the arsenal of unarmed combat techniques belonging to a Teräs Käsi Master. It consisted of a sideways flip, bringing one's feet down on the opponent three times before bashing with both fists at the same time in a vertical fashion.
*[[Steel hands]] was a technique which was eponymous with the martial art itself.
*[[Striking Sarlacc]] was named after the dreaded [[Sarlacc/Legends|Sarlacc]].

==Behind the scenes==
Teräs Käsi is inspired by a real-life fighting style called [[Wikipedia:Pencak silat|pencak silat]],<ref name="SP interview">{{WebCite|url=http://www.teraskasi.net/sperry_051706_01.htm|text=Steve Perry Talks Teräs Käsi, Walks Silat Serak|accessdate=2014-02-01|author=Taigei|date=2005-06-17|work=teraskasi.net|archivedate=20080211224053}}</ref> with the word Teräs Käsi coming from the real world [[Wikipedia:Finnish language|Finnish]] language. Translated word for word in Finnish, Teräs Käsi means "steel hand" as opposed to the plural "steel hands" - this has been retconned in canon somewhat by having sources say both "hand" or "hands". The name Teräs Käsi meaning "steel hand" is an allusion to the video game series ''[[W:c:tekken:Tekken (series)|Tekken]]'' by [[Namco]], which was a direct source of inspiration for the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Masters of Teräs Käsi]]''. In [[Steve Perry]]'s novel ''The Musashi Flex'', a prequel to his Matador book series, Teräs Käsi is briefly mentioned as one of the fighting styles practiced by the novel's main character.
